topics.title: Chapter 24 — Kernel and Hardware Administration
topics.summary: Applications depend on a kernel, drivers, and hardware that must be understood as a layered system. topics.title: 24.1 Kernel Architecture
topics.summary: The Linux kernel manages execution, memory, devices, filesystems, and networking, and exposes interfaces used by user-space programs. Drivers and many other facilities can be built into the kernel or supplied as loadable modules. A userspace service and a kernel component operate with different boundaries and failure consequences.

blocks.text: The Linux kernel manages execution, memory, devices, filesystems, and networking, and exposes interfaces used by user-space programs. Drivers and many other facilities can be built into the kernel or supplied as loadable modules. A userspace service and a kernel component operate with different boundaries and failure consequences.

A system call is an application request to the kernel for a protected operation, such as opening a file or creating a process. A hardware interrupt signals an event requiring attention. You do not need to write kernel code to administer a server, but knowing which layer handles an operation helps locate failures. (R01)

Avoid interpreting every application crash as a kernel fault. A segmentation fault in one process usually calls first for that application’s diagnostics; a kernel panic or widespread device errors suggests a different scope.
Linux example — 24.1
Inspect kernel identity and exposed subsystems.

uname -a
ls /sys/class

blocks.text: The command line can reveal boot parameters relevant to a problem; review it before sharing because environments may include sensitive details. Record architecture and package provenance as well as the release string.

Do not decide vulnerability status by comparing only a vendor kernel’s visible version with an upstream announcement. Use the applicable distribution advisory and installed package build. Keep old recovery kernels according to a controlled retention policy rather than removing every alternative immediately after an update.

topics.title: 24.3 Kernel Modules
topics.summary: A module adds kernel functionality at runtime when supported. Storage, network, filesystem, and virtualization features may use modules. Their dependencies, signatures, version compatibility, and configuration determine whether they load correctly.

blocks.text: A module adds kernel functionality at runtime when supported. Storage, network, filesystem, and virtualization features may use modules. Their dependencies, signatures, version compatibility, and configuration determine whether they load correctly.

A loaded module executes with kernel privilege, so its provenance matters. Prefer supported distribution packages and approved vendor drivers. Copying a module from a different kernel build can fail or create an unsupported environment.

Modules built into the kernel do not appear as ordinary loaded modules. Absence from lsmod therefore does not prove a feature is unavailable. Inspect kernel configuration and device binding through appropriate tools before concluding that a driver is missing.
Linux example — 24.3
List modules and inspect one common module's metadata.

lsmod
modinfo loop

blocks.text: Kernel parameters can come from the boot command line or runtime interfaces. Some take effect only at boot; others change live behavior. The presence of a similarly named sysctl does not make the two mechanisms interchangeable.

Before changing a parameter, record its purpose, current value, scope, supported values, workload effect, and rollback. An option copied from a low-latency trading system can be inappropriate for a general-purpose VM.

Use an experiment with a measurable outcome. “Increase performance” is too vague. “Reduce a measured queue bottleneck without raising error rate or resource use beyond agreed limits” provides something to test.

Read boot arguments and one runtime parameter.

cat /proc/cmdline
sysctl vm.swappiness

blocks.text: sysctl reads and writes runtime kernel settings exposed through supported interfaces, commonly represented under /proc/sys. A read does not imply that changing the value is safe.

sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward

blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: Use individual keys for focused investigation. A blanket sysctl -a can produce large output, permission warnings, and irrelevant information. Persistent settings normally belong in a reviewed file under /etc/sysctl.d, subject to precedence and the system’s loader.

A runtime write and persistent configuration must be verified separately. sysctl --system can apply many configured settings, not just the one you edited. For a bounded change, understand exactly which keys your chosen application command will touch. (R53)
Linux example — 24.7
Read a sysctl value without changing it.

sysctl vm.swappiness
sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward
# Runtime change syntax; record the original value and an approved workload first:
# sudo sysctl -w vm.swappiness=20
# Restore the recorded original value after the bounded experiment.

topics.title: 24.9 Hardware Discovery
topics.summary: Hardware discovery creates an inventory connecting a physical or virtual device to its bus address, driver, firmware, operating-system name, and role. A drive name such as /dev/sdb is not a sufficient asset identity, especially after reordering or replacement.

concepts.definition: Hardware discovery creates an inventory connecting a physical or virtual device to its bus address, driver, firmware, operating-system name, and role. A drive name such as /dev/sdb is not a sufficient asset identity, especially after reordering or replacement.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Guests may expose virtual hardware; missing tools require package inspection.

blocks.text: Hardware discovery creates an inventory connecting a physical or virtual device to its bus address, driver, firmware, operating-system name, and role. A drive name such as /dev/sdb is not a sufficient asset identity, especially after reordering or replacement.

Use lsblk for block-device relationships, lspci for PCI devices, lsusb for USB devices, and lscpu for CPU topology. Some information requires elevated access. Firmware tools can expose serial numbers and other identifiers that should be protected when sharing reports.

Compare the expected inventory with what the running system sees. A missing device may be disabled in firmware, detached from a VM, unsupported by a driver, or failed physically. Those possibilities precede filesystem-level repair.
Linux example — 24.9
Inventory hardware tools' observations.

lscpu
lsblk -d -o NAME,MODEL,SIZE
lspci

blocks.text: lscpu reports architecture and topology such as sockets, cores, threads, and NUMA nodes. A virtual CPU count is not a direct guarantee of dedicated physical cores. CPU features exposed to a guest depend on the hypervisor and migration policy.

Use topology to interpret per-core performance and placement, not as a reason to pin every service arbitrarily. Pinning can reduce scheduler flexibility and create contention. Chapter 30 considers NUMA and high-performance tradeoffs.

Record whether the workload uses a single thread, several workers, or vector instructions. Adding CPUs does not make serial work parallel. A correct capacity plan connects the program’s concurrency to the available execution resources.

Inspect CPU topology and capabilities.

lscpu
getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN

blocks.text: Memory information includes total capacity, available capacity, topology, and hardware error evidence. /proc/meminfo describes the kernel’s view; firmware inventory tools can describe installed modules when the platform exposes that information.

A difference between installed and usable memory can result from hardware reservations, virtualization, kernel settings, or faults. Do not infer failure solely from a rounded number. Compare exact units and the platform’s expected reservations.

Where supported, hardware error logs and vendor management interfaces can help investigate corrected and uncorrected memory errors. Replacement decisions need the platform’s service procedure and evidence, not a generic “memory is high” alert.

topics.title: 24.14 Device Problems
topics.summary: Start with the device’s role and failure scope. An application timeout may result from link loss, driver resets, media errors, path failover, or power. Correlate the kernel log with storage or network metrics and any hardware-management records.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Correlate the device ID, driver, and error time before replacing hardware.

blocks.text: Start with the device’s role and failure scope. An application timeout may result from link loss, driver resets, media errors, path failover, or power. Correlate the kernel log with storage or network metrics and any hardware-management records.

Protect data before invasive tests. A full-disk stress test on a suspect production drive can worsen a fragile situation and affect users. Read-only diagnostics can still impose load; schedule them with the device owner.

When replacing hardware, verify stable identities and mappings before bringing services back. The replacement may enumerate under a different name. A previously correct /dev/sdX assumption is not a safe provisioning contract.
Linux example — 24.14
Look for device-related kernel warnings.

sudo journalctl -k -b -p warning -n 60 --no-pager
lspci -nnk

topics.title: 24.15 Kernel Updates
topics.summary: Treat a kernel update as a change that requires installed-package validation, boot selection, driver compatibility, and a planned restart unless a supported live-patching mechanism covers the exact issue. Live patching is not a blanket replacement for all kernel maintenance.

cards.question: What should you check after this section’s example?
cards.answer: Preserve a tested recovery kernel and console path before applying a reviewed kernel update.

blocks.text: Treat a kernel update as a change that requires installed-package validation, boot selection, driver compatibility, and a planned restart unless a supported live-patching mechanism covers the exact issue. Live patching is not a blanket replacement for all kernel maintenance.

Confirm backups, console access, known-good boot entries, and application acceptance tests before the window. Account for externally built modules, Secure Boot requirements, and storage drivers needed during early boot.

After restart, record uname -r, failed units, storage, networking, and the real application test. A successful package-manager transaction before reboot is not evidence that the new kernel booted or that the service works under it.
Linux example — 24.15
Record the preupdate boot state.

uname -r
df -h /boot
ls /boot

blocks.title: Original Linux example

blocks.text: Permissions and persistent-journal configuration affect visibility. For intermittent panics, establish the distribution’s supported crash-dump arrangement before the next event. Crash artifacts can contain sensitive memory and need restricted handling.

Escalate with observations, reproduction conditions, and recent changes. Avoid inventing a hardware diagnosis from an isolated warning. A good report distinguishes the first abnormal event from the downstream failures it triggered.
Linux example — 24.16
Collect a bounded kernel diagnostic snapshot.

uname -a
cat /proc/cmdline
sudo journalctl -k -b -n 80 --no-pager

blocks.text: Record whether the host is meant to forward traffic, which interfaces exist, and what firewall policy assumes. Serving a local web socket does not require acting as a router. In this scenario the correct administrative action is to reject the unrelated change and preserve the observed baseline.

For a separate disposable router lab, define two isolated networks, explicit forwarding and firewall requirements, approved test traffic, and console recovery. Only then plan a temporary change, a discriminating connectivity test, restoration of the original value, and a persistent configuration if the design is accepted.
This exercise teaches that administration includes choosing not to mutate the system. A documented decision with a mechanism is more valuable than an unexplained tuning line.

labs.title: Keep installed and running kernel versions separate
labs.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
lab_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$lab_dir"' EXIT
cd -- "$lab_dir"
printf 'installed=version-B\nrunning=version-A\n' > kernel.fixture
installed=$(sed -n 's/^installed=//p' kernel.fixture)
running=$(sed -n 's/^running=//p' kernel.fixture)
test "$installed" != "$running"
printf 'installed and running versions differ\n'
